stem: Maximum strength of Lok Sabha as stipulated in the Constitution of India is -

stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The President of India can summon a session of the Parliament at such place as he / she thinks fit.
2. The Constitution of India provides for three sessions of the Parliament in a year, but it is not mandatory to conduct all three sessions.
3. There is no minimum number of days that the parliament is required to meet in a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Article 85(1) of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. So, the constitution provides for the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament but there is no minimum gap. Hence, statements 1 and 3 are correct, while statement 2 is wrong. So the correct answer is option (c).

stem: Generally how many sessions are there in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Article 85 of the Constitution of India deals with the session, prorogation and dissolution of the Parliament. Under this, the President is given the power to call the session of each House of the Parliament from time to time, provided that the session of Parliament should be called by the President in such a way that there should not be a gap of 6 months between the last meeting of one session and the first meeting of the next session. In other words, at least two sessions of the Parliament should be called in a year. By the way, the three sessions of the Lok Sabha, usually called in a year in India are– 1. Budget Session (February – May) 2. Monsoon Session (July – August) 3. Winter Session (November – December)

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the election for Lok Sabha or State Assembly, the winning candidate must get at least 50 percent of the votes polled, to be declared elected.
2. According to the provisions laid down in the Constitution of India, in Lok Sabha, the Speaker's post goes to the majority party and the Deputy Speaker's to the Opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: The election for Lok Sabha or state Assembly in India is conducted on the principle of 'First past the Post System'. In this method, the candidate with the highest number (but not necessarily a majority) of votes is elected. Thus, statement 1 is incorrect. According to Article 93 of the Constitution, "the House of the people shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Traditionally, the speaker's post goes to the majority and the Deputy speaker to the Opposition. However, there is no such provision in the constitution. Therefore, statement 2 is also wrong.

options.text: A resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a majority of the members of the House.

options.label: b
options.text: Two third majority of the members of the House.

options.label: d
options.text: A simple majority of the Parliament.

expl: The procedure for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha has been made under Article 94(c). The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker may be removed from his office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen (14) days' notice has been given to the Speaker of the intention to move the resolution.

stem:
With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements : While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration
1. He/She shall not preside.
2. He/She shall not have the right to speak.
3. He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: As per Article 96 (1) of the Constitution of India, "At any sitting of the House of the People, while any resolution for the removal of the Speaker from his office is under consideration, the Speaker, or while any resolution for the removal of the Deputy Speaker from his office is under consideration, the Deputy Speaker, shall not, though he is present, preside, and the provisions of Clause (2) of Article 95 shall apply in relation to every such sitting as they apply in relation to a sitting from which the Speaker, or, as the case may be, the Deputy Speaker, is absent." Hence, statement 1 is correct. As per Article 96 (2), "The Speaker shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, the House of the People while any resolution for his removal from office is under consideration in the House and shall, notwithstanding anything in article 100, be entitled to vote only in the first instance on such resolution or on any other matter during such proceedings but not in the case of an equality of votes." Hence, statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.

stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution.
II. According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political party immediately.
III. The Speaker of the House of the People may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
expl: The provisions regarding vacation, resignation and removal from the offices of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are given in Article 94 of the Indian Constitution. In the second proviso to the same Article, it is clearly stated that when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the Speaker shall not vacate his office on such dissolution, and shall continue in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha. Therefore, Statement I is correct. The Constitution nowhere mentions that a member of the Lok Sabha, upon being elected as Speaker, must compulsorily resign from his political party immediately. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha; such a resolution cannot be moved in the Lok Sabha unless at least 14 days’ notice of the intention to move the resolution has been given. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

stem: Which one of the following statements regarding the office of the Speaker is correct?

options.label: a
options.text: He holds office during the pleasure of the President.

options.label: b
options.text: He need not be a member of the House at the time of his election but has to become a member of the House within six months from the date of his election.

options.label: c
options.text: he loses his office if the house is dissolved before the end of its normal tenure.

options.label: d
options.text: If he intends to resign the letter of his resignation is to be addressed to the Deputy Speaker.

expl: According to Article 94, the Speaker must be a member of the House at the time of his election for the office. The Speaker may be removed by a resolution of a majority of members of the House. According to Article 94, whenever the House is dissolved, the Speaker shall not vacate his office until immediately before the first meeting of the Lok Sabha after the dissolution. According to Article 94(b), if the Speaker intends to resign, the letter of his resignation is to be addressed to the Deputy Speaker. So, in the given statements, (a), (b), and (c) are wrong, and statement (d) is correct.

stem:
Regarding the office of the Lok Sabha Speaker, consider the following statements:
1. He/She holds the office during the pleasure of the President.
2. He/She need not be a member of the House at the time of his/her election but has to become a member of the House within six months from the date of his/ her election.
3. If he/she intends to resign, the letter of his/her resignation has to be addressed to the Deputy Speaker.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
expl: The Speaker of the House of the People shall be chosen by the members of the Lok Sabha among themselves. He may be removed from the office by a resolution passed by the majority of all the then members of the House. The Speaker may address his resignation to the Deputy Speaker of the House.

stem: Which of the following statement is not true about the speaker of Lok Sabha?

options.label: a
options.text: Speaker has to be the member of the house within six months, he assumes office.

options.label: b
options.text: He remains speaker so long as he member of the house.

options.label: c
options.text: Speaker continues in office even if Lok Sabha is dissolved.

options.label: d
options.text: Speaker can be removed by the members of Lok Sabha.

expl: According to the Article 93 of the Constitution, The House of the People chooses two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Therefore, no person, who is not a member of the House, can be chosen Speaker or Deputy Speaker. Under Article 94 clause (c) the Speaker or Deputy Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) passed by a majority of all the then members of the House. Speaker or Deputy Speaker vacates his office if he ceases to be a member of the House [Article 94(a)] . According to the second proviso of the Article 94, whenever the House of the People is dissolved, the speaker shall not vacate his office, until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after dissolution.

expl: As soon as the new Government is formed, the Legislative section of the Parliament prepares a list of the senior-most Lok Sabha members, and one of them is appointed as pro-tem Speaker. The function of pro-tem Speaker is to administer the oath to the newly elected members of the House and conduct proceedings till a regular Speaker is chosen.

options.label: c

expl: As soon as the new Government is formed, the legislative section of parliament prepares a list of the senior-most Lok Sabha members. This list is then submitted to the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs for the appointment of pro-tem Speaker. Thereafter, the minister submits a note to the President seeking his approval for the appointment of the pro-tem Speaker.

stem:
Which of the following statements regarding the powers of the speaker of Lok Sabha are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
(i) The speaker presides over a joint sitting of both the houses of Parliament.
(ii) When a Money Bill is transferred from the Lower House to the Upper House, the speaker shall endorse on the bill his certificate that it is a Money Bill.
(iii) While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the speaker shall neither preside nor take part in its proceedings.
(iv) The speaker does not vote in the House except when there is equality of votes.
Codes :
expl: The President summons the joint sitting of the Houses of the Parliament (under Article 108).The Speaker of the House of the People presides over a joint sitting of both the Houses of Parliament under Article 118(4). Under Article 110(4) every Money Bill shall be endorsed, When it is transmitted to the Council of States under Article 109, and when it is presented to the President for assent under Article 111 the certificate of the Speaker of the House of the People, signed by him that it is a Money Bill. Under Article 96, while a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the Speaker shall not preside, but he can take part in its proceedings, shall have the right to speak and the right to vote in the first instance and not in the case of equality of votes. Hence, the Statement (iii) is incorrect. According to Article 100(1), the Chairman or speaker, or person acting as such, shall not vote in the first instance, but shall exercise a casting vote (deciding vote) in the case of an equality of votes.

stem: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha enjoys

options.label: a
options.text: The right to vote only in case of a tie

options.label: b
options.text: The right to vote like other members of the House

options.label: c
options.text: Two votes - one in ordinary course and the other in case of a tie

expl: According to Article 100(1) of the Constitution, All questions at any sitting of either House or joint sitting of the Houses shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, excluding the speaker or person acting as chairman or speaker. The Speaker or chairman, or person acting as such, shall not vote in first instance. But shall exercise a casting vote in the case of equality of votes (i.e. a tie) and hence decide the matter. In this case, the Speaker's vote will count. According to an additional provision under Article 96(1), if the Speaker's position is challenged by a motion in the Lok Sabha, they will continue to remain in their position until the motion is disposed of. According to Article 96(2), in such cases, if there is a motion of no confidence against the Speaker, they will not be allowed to vote during the debate on the motion, as their presence will not influence the vote. However, during other matters, the Speaker is entitled to cast their vote in case of a tie. This right is known as the casting vote. The Speaker may also delegate this casting vote to other members of the House.

stem: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha makes use of his casting vote only –

options.label: d
options.text: In case of a tie when votes are equally divided

expl: Article 100 (1) of the Constitution provides a procedure for voting in the Houses. Any question at any sitting shall be decided by a majority of votes of the members present and voting. According to 100(1), the Speaker or person acting as Chairman or Speaker, shall not vote in the first instance, but shall have and exercise a ‘’casting vote’’ in the case of an equality of votes. Article 96 gives a different exercise of casting a vote by the Speaker. According to Article 96(2), the Speaker shall have the right to cast a vote in the first instance on the question of resolution for his removal, but not in the case of equality of votes.

stem: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha ?
expl: G. V. Mavalankar became the first Speaker of the First Lok Sabha of independent India on 15 May 1952 and remained in office until his death on 27 February 1956. He is also known as the “Father of the Lok Sabha” for laying the foundations of parliamentary procedure, rules, and traditions. This title was conferred on him by J.L. Nehru.

stem:
With reference to Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. As per the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the election of Deputy Speaker shall be held on such date as the Speaker may fix.
2. There is a mandatory provision that the election of a candidate as Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha shall be from either the principal opposition party or the ruling party.
3. The Deputy Speaker has the same power as of the Speaker when presiding over the sitting of the House and no appeal lies against his rulings.
4. The well established parliamentary practice regarding the appointment of Deputy Speaker is that the motion is moved by the Speaker and duly seconded by the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
expl: As per Rule 8(1) of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha, the election of the Deputy Speaker shall be held on such date as the Speaker may fix and the secretary convey to all members. As per Article 93, the speaker and deputy speaker of the House of the People shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House, respectively. There is no mandatory provision that the election of candidates as Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha shall be from either the principal opposition or ruling party. Article 95(1) of the Indian Constitution, in the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker chairs the house and he has the same power as the speaker when presiding over the sitting of the house and no appeal lies against his rulings. As per rule 8(2) of the Rule of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha a motion regarding the appointment of the deputy speaker is moved by one member and seconded by another member. Thus statement (4) is also wrong.

options.label: d
options.text: President aftern consultation with the Speaker of the House of the people

expl: At the administrative level, the authority to issue appointment orders lies with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whereas the constitutional power to frame rules for this entire structure, under Article 98(3), lies with the President, who makes rules after consultation with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. If viewed purely as “who issues the individual appointment orders”, then under Rule 6 of the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1955, the answer would be “the Speaker of the Lok Sabha”, but this option is not given separately in the choices.

stem: In which year the number of women member of Parliament was the lowest in Lok Sabha?
expl: The lowest number of women elected to Lok Sabha was in 1977, when only 19 women reached the lower house. In the General Election 2019, the highest number of women reached to the Lok Sabha (78).

stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. In the first Lok Sabha, the single largest party in the opposition was the Swatantra Party.
2. In the Lok Sabha, a "Leader of the Opposition" was recognised for the first time in 1969.
3. In the Lok Sabha, if a party does not have a minimum of 75 members, its leader cannot be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: * The first Lok Sabha elections were conducted for 489 seats, out of which the Indian National Congress (INC) won 364 seats and emerged as the single largest party. * Second place was secured by the Communist Party of India with 16 seats. * It was only in 1969, that a 'leader of opposition' was recognised. Till then, the practice was to call the leader of the party in opposition, having the largest number of members as the leader of the opposition, without having any formal recognition, status or privilege. *However, in order to get formal recognition, the concerned party must have at least 10% of the total strength of the House i.e. 55 seats in the Lok Sabha.
